public_rationale: The reviewed evidence documents working accelerators and substantial cloud revenue, but does not establish either population-wide majority. Idle GPU-hours do not mean GPUs are physically warehoused. Cloud revenue also does not identify how many purchasing companies have earned substantial revenue from their GPUs. The evidence therefore neither supports nor disproves the two asserted majorities.
limitations: Operational-fleet telemetry excludes hardware that has not been installed.
An individual company's results cannot establish a majority by buyer count.
The selected quarter does not capture all changes before September 22.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The vast majority of companies that have bought GPUs have yet to turn them into meaningful revenue, if they have turned them on at all, and most of NVIDIA's sales are sitting in warehouses.

statement.excerpt: I need to be more blunt here: the vast majority of companies that have bought GPUs have yet to turn them into meaningful revenue, if they’ve turned them on at all. Most of NVIDIA’s sales are sitting in warehouses, and that is a significant disclosure that NVIDIA should have already been forced to make.

from_speaker: the vast majority of companies that have bought GPUs
have yet to turn them into meaningful revenue
if they’ve turned them on at all
Most of NVIDIA’s sales are sitting in warehouses
our_interpretation: The context concerns AI GPUs, rather than consumer graphics purchases.
Read 'vast majority of companies' by company count and 'meaningful revenue' as substantial realized revenue attributable to GPU use; profitability is a separate question.
Read the warehouse assertion as more than half of sold AI GPU hardware remaining physically stored and undeployed. Unit count and sales value are plausible alternative denominators.
Use calendar Q2 2026, the latest completed common customer reporting quarter before the post, for the ongoing deployment and revenue state.
Exclude the normative demand that NVIDIA should have been forced to disclose this.
criteria.support_condition: A representative purchaser census establishes that a large majority lack substantial GPU-generated revenue, and shipment-to-deployment records establish that over half of the relevant sold hardware remains warehoused.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative records establish that either asserted majority is false. Examples of successful buyers or installed clusters alone are insufficient.

evidence.explanation: The study covers operating accelerator telemetry through June 2026. Its installed-fleet sample and GPU-hour denominator cannot establish the share of sold NVIDIA hardware in warehouses or the share of buyers earning substantial revenue.

Microsoft reports substantial realized cloud revenue, but this includes services beyond purchased GPUs. Neither that revenue nor the separate future performance obligations settle the buyer-wide claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative purchaser survey or census linked to shipment cohorts, installation status and realized GPU-attributable revenue, with explicit denominators and accounting definitions.
